entries.reason: Dialogue is the consumer that owns these two contracts: DialogueState::queryProviders walks cap::query and then cap::forEach for IStateQuery, and DialogueStateContext::apply takes IStateMutation through cap::query. The new script seams answer the first as a listener and the second in the single-provider slot, so both faces appear here and the next provider must declare itself instead of silently displacing the slot. The scope is this one file, not src/modules/dialogue/**: the runner, parser and bindings expose different faces.
binds: eve.provider.publishFor('eve.state.IStateQuery', name, instance) -> value/hasTag/attribute/resource/state/authority(subject, key|tag|scope), null meaning 'not mine'; eve.provider.publishFor('eve.state.IStateMutation', name, instance) -> applyStateMutations({ transactionId, correlationId, causationId, mutations = [{ subject, key, value, kind, persistent }] }) returning the number of changed entries
entries.thread_affinity: Squirrel owning thread; the seam answers IStateQuery and IStateMutation synchronously while a dialogue expression is evaluated and retains no VM value between calls

trim.absent_profile: Profiles without dialogue drop the seams; other IStateQuery/IStateMutation providers keep answering through the same forEach walk, so dialogue state resolution degrades to the remaining providers

cost_notes: Each value/hasTag/attribute/resource/state/authority call is one script call that returns null for 'not mine', so the walk continues; applyStateMutations marshals one mutation table per batch.
